slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 16, treat 16.1.1 Implementing Insertion and Selection Sort as an algorithmic claim. Insertion sort maintains a sorted prefix [0,i). Save the value at i, shift larger prefix values one position right, and place the saved value in the resulting gap. During the shift, the saved local value prevents it from being overwritten. The condition checks j>0 before reading index j-1. The comparison uses strict less-than, so a value is not shifted past an equal predecessor. This makes the algorithm stable when generalized to records under a consistent comparator: equal-key records retain their input order. Stability is about distinguishable equal-key records, not about identical integers alone. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. slides.title: 16.2.1 Implementing Merge Sort
keyPoints: Merge sort divides a half-open range into two smaller ranges until each has at most one element.
After recursively sorting both halves, merge them by repeatedly selecting the smaller remaining front value.
Every selected value is the smallest still available across both sorted halves, which proves the output prefix.
When keys are equal, the code selects from the left half.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 16, treat 16.2.1 Implementing Merge Sort as an algorithmic claim. Merge sort divides a half-open range into two smaller ranges until each has at most one element. After recursively sorting both halves, merge them by repeatedly selecting the smaller remaining front value. Every selected value is the smallest still available across both sorted halves, which proves the output prefix remains sorted. When keys are equal, the code selects from the left half. That tie rule preserves stability across the split. A reusable temporary vector is allocated once outside recursion; each merge writes its range into the temporary storage and copies it back. The implementation uses O(n) auxiliary element storage and O(log n) call depth. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. slides.title: Failure clinic — Sorted output lost a value
keyPoints: A candidate output is nondecreasing but contains a duplicate replacing a missing value.
An is_sorted check alone passes.
Compare the full output with a sorted copy of the original or independently verify the multiset.
Sorting correctness includes preservation, not just final order.
slides.narration: In Book III, Chapter 16, treat Failure clinic — Sorted output lost a value as an algorithmic claim. A candidate output is nondecreasing but contains a duplicate replacing a missing value. An is_sorted check alone passes. Compare the full output with a sorted copy of the original or independently verify the multiset. Sorting correctness includes preservation, not just final order. A quick-sort partition occasionally leaves one high value among the low region. Inspect whether current advanced after swapping from the greater region. The incoming value still belongs to the unknown region and must be classified before advancing. A merge reads beyond one half near the final output positions. Check exhaustion conditions before comparing front values. Once one half is empty, only the other can supply remaining values. A comparison expression with unsafe evaluation order can dereference an exhausted side even when another condition would have selected the right branch. At a graduate level, the answer is never just that the code ran. Ask what invariant is preserved, what state changes, why termination follows, what input size controls cost, and what output or diagnostic proves the implementation matched the specification.
